text:
The Islanders have had back-to-back hat tricks: Simon Holmstrom against Anaheim, then Matthew Schaefer against Columbus on Tuesday. Schaefer is the reason people are watching. He has 15 points in his last 10 games, a six-game point streak, and Stefen Rosner of The Elmonters wrote this week that he is "showing everyone what greatness looks like." Our form check calls his run earned, because the chances have come with it, and we have him at 38% for two or more points tonight, the best mark on the Islanders.

The rest of the Islanders' story needs a footnote. They have won three straight and are 3-0-2 in five, but with 46% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in those games and 46% on the season. A +9 goal difference on a -9.1 expected one is mostly goaltending, 14.7 goals saved above expected, plus some hot finishing. Tonight Ilya Sorokin sits and Semyon Varlamov starts; he has been excellent in a small sample, +5.7 in six games. Mathew Barzal is easing back after a knee problem he called the hardest journey of his life, and Logan Stanley returns to Winnipeg after 261 games as a Jet.

Winnipeg also goes to its backup. Nico Daws starts over Stuart Skinner, with an even 0.0 against expected in eight games. The Jets' six-game streak ended Tuesday in a 2-1 loss to Ottawa, the one game in the run where they were clearly outplayed (31% of the chances). Before that they took 52% or better in four straight. Mark Scheifele is now the franchise's points leader after a four-point night in Chicago, Nino Niederreiter is one point from 500 and Alex Iafallo one from 300. Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve.

Our numbers have it close, 3.25 expected goals for Winnipeg to 3.06 for New York. Kyle Connor is 49% to score, the highest on the board in this game. Our sleepers are Jets: Viggo Björck, fresh off his first NHL goal, at 15% to score, and Cole Perfetti at 57% for a point.
headline: Matthew Schaefer, and a pair of backups, in Winnipeg
